title: Scientists using LLMs will ‘do more, less well’, modelling study predicts
excerpt: Research suggests that the combination of incentives to publish and the use of large language models will lead to more papers, but they will be less refined.
content_html:
• NEWS
  • 31 July 2026

Research suggests that the combination of incentives to publish and the use of large language models will lead to more papers, but they will be less refined.

By

  • Kaia Glickman
  1. Kaia Glickman

Scientists who use large language models (LLMs) to help them with their research will spend less time refining their work and instead jump quickly to fresh projects, according to a modelling study1.

Adoption of LLMs will cause scientists to “do more, less well — rather than the same amount, better”, write the authors. But they say that such artificial-intelligence tools do not bear all of the blame for that outcome.

The results reflect a flawed incentive system in science that prioritizes quantity over quality, says study co-author Carl Bergstrom, a biologist at the University of Washington in Seattle. Scientists are incentivized to churn out papers, he says, and LLMs help them to reach this ever-growing quota. “LLMs are rarely the problem themselves,” says Bergstrom. “LLMs hold up a mirror to problems that we already have.” The study was posted on the arXiv preprint repository on 19 July and has not yet been peer reviewed.

Foraging for papers

To predict how LLMs will change scientific productivity, the authors broke the research process into discrete phases. First comes a discovery phase when scientists brainstorm hypotheses and conduct initial experiments to determine the value of a project. Next, there is a two-part development phase that consists of required work (such as creating figures and drafting papers) and discretionary development (such as conducting follow-up experiments and polishing writing).

The authors drew on methods from optimal-foraging theory — which analyses how an animal maximizes energy gain while conserving resources — to analyse how scientists will reallocate their efforts after incorporating LLMs into their work. The authors’ model assumed LLMs are functioning at their best — cheap, fast and accurate.

AI linked to explosion of low-quality biomedical research papers

The modelling predicts that LLMs can speed up all phases of the scientific process, but that this acceleration won’t result in better papers. Faster discovery and required-work phases mean that researchers can churn out papers more quickly than they could without the help of LLMs, and the pressure to publish means there is little incentive to spend extra time polishing those papers.

Quality not quantity

content_html_zh:
• NEWS
  • 31 July 2026

研究表明，发表激励措施和大型语言模型的使用相结合将导致论文数量增多，但论文的精炼度会降低。

By

  • 凯亚格利克曼
  1. 凯亚格利克曼

一项建模研究表明，使用大型语言模型 (LLM) 来帮助他们进行研究的科学家将花费更少的时间完善他们的工作，而是快速跳转到新的项目。

作者写道，采用法学硕士将导致科学家“做得更多，做得更少——而不是等量做得更好”。 但他们表示，这种人工智能工具并不能承担这一结果的全部责任。

该研究的合著者、西雅图华盛顿大学的生物学家卡尔·伯格斯特罗姆说，这些结果反映出科学界的激励制度存在缺陷，这种制度优先考虑数量而不是质量。 他说，科学家们被激励大量发表论文，而法学硕士帮助他们达到这一不断增长的配额。 “法学硕士本身很少是问题，”伯格斯特罗姆说。 “法学硕士为我们已经存在的问题提供了一面镜子。” 该研究于 7 月 19 日发布在 arXiv 预印本存储库上，尚未经过同行评审。

寻找论文

为了预测法学硕士将如何改变科学生产力，作者将研究过程分为不同的阶段。 首先是发现阶段，科学家们集体讨论假设并进行初步实验以确定项目的价值。 接下来，有一个由两部分组成的开发阶段，包括必需的工作（例如创建图形和起草论文）和酌情开发（例如进行后续实验和润色写作）。

作者利用最佳觅食理论（该理论分析动物如何在节约资源的同时最大化能量增益）的方法来分析科学家在将法学硕士纳入他们的工作后将如何重新分配他们的努力。 作者的模型假设法学硕士处于最佳状态——廉价、快速且准确。

人工智能与低质量生物医学研究论文的激增有关

该模型预测法学硕士可以加速科学过程的所有阶段，但这种加速不会产生更好的论文。 更快的发现和所需的工作阶段意味着研究人员可以比没有法学硕士的帮助更快地发表论文，而发表的压力意味着没有动力花额外的时间润色这些论文。
